conviction_note: Magnitude anchor built by hand, not inherited: 6 of the baseline's 8 dates map to MAMA's Jan-31 fiscal quarter ends and are genuine prints (-11.1, -0.3, +28.1, -4.9, +0.7, -0.3; median |move| 2.8%, last-four mean |move| 11.1%), while 2025-09-02 is verifiably the Crown I acquisition/private-placement 8-K and not a print - cross-checked against the front-expiry straddle (9.4%, but 526 total OI and a 55%-of-mid ATM spread, so indicative only); I used ~8% as the plausible magnitude and took roughly a third of it to the upside, because the mechanically favourable shape of this specific quarter is being met by a -15.8% 20-day tape with no disclosed company event behind it.

findings.finding: The two inputs nobody watching MAMA is tracking are benign in exactly this quarter: CME 40-lb block cheddar closed $1.5050/lb on 2026-07-08, near the bottom of its own 2022-2026 $1.30-$2.40 range, and retail boneless chicken breast averaged $4.15/lb in July 2026, down 1.2% year over year with breast-meat supply called balanced-to-heavy through end-2026 - so the Q1 gross-margin shortfall the market de-rated the stock for, which the CFO quantified on the June 8 call as ~$0.5-1.0m of one-time launch labour/material inefficiency plus ~$0.5m reclassified from marketing to trade, was not a commodity problem and does not have a commodity reason to repeat.
findings.why_not_priced: The published bear narrative on this name is single-input: record beef, because beef meatballs are the flagship SKU and beef inflation is front-page. MAMA discloses no input basket, so nobody has priced the offsets. If the market had done the basket, the June de-rating would have been followed by margin-recovery notes rather than by two fresh Buy/Outperform initiations at $22-25 into a stock that then fell another 16%; and the option chain would not be showing 0.61 put/call open interest with no measurable 25-delta skew on a name whose only live controversy is gross margin.
findings.independence: Second, different source on the other input: retail boneless chicken breast $4.15/lb in July 2026, -1.2% YoY, https://basketreport.com/prices/chicken-breast/ . I am deliberately NOT putting a beef number in this finding - every dated beef figure I could reach sat on an undated trade-press URL I could not pin to 2026 rather than 2025, and record beef is the acknowledged offset that keeps this finding's low end negative.

findings.finding: Fiscal Q2 (May 1 - Jul 31 2026) is the first full quarter of revenue from the 2,000 Walmart and 750 Target deli doors, which management said on 2026-06-08 'did not launch till the middle to end of April - so we had all the costs... The cost is all in Q1. But really, very little of the revenue was in Q1' - i.e. the costs and the revenue were split across the quarter boundary in the company's favour, and the market has sold the stock 15.8% in 20 sessions into that split with no company news since the 2026-08-20 earnings-date notice.
findings.why_not_priced: The quote is public, which is why I size this small. What is not public is that nothing has happened since: the EDGAR filing index shows no filing of any kind after 2026-07-31 (a Vanguard 13G) and the IR page lists no release after 2026-08-20, so the 13% slide from $17.67 on 2026-08-10 to $15.365 has no disclosed company event behind it and is not information. If the market were pricing the cost/revenue split it would not have the stock 25.6% off its high and 15% below the $18.00 offering price struck on 2026-06-30, with short interest falling 18% (i.e. not a short raid) and no insider selling on file.
findings.independence: Timing corroborated from a different source - the 2026-05-04 PR Newswire launch release dating the 2,000 Walmart / 750 Target deli rollout, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mamas-creations-redefines-the-modern-deli-experience-with-major-national-retail-expansion-302761049.html . Note this finding shares the EDGAR filing-index observation with the M&A finding below; collapse the two to one source cluster if scoring by document.

findings.finding: MAMA raised $94m net at $18.00/share on 2026-06-30 explicitly to fund 'the acquisition of businesses or other assets', has filed no 8-K item 1.01/2.01 in the two months since, and has form for announcing deals into this exact calendar slot: on 2026's equivalent week last year it filed the Crown I asset purchase plus a $20m private placement (8-K dated 2025-09-02, event 2025-08-28) six days before the Q2 print and the stock moved +14.4% that day.
findings.why_not_priced: This is only visible by reading the EDGAR index against the use-of-proceeds language in the 424B5 and noticing the two-month gap - no aggregator carries 'cash raised for M&A, not yet spent'. If it were priced, the front expiry would not sit at 526 total contracts of open interest; a live M&A-announcement possibility on a $700m name would show up as call open interest well above 320 contracts and a negative 25-delta skew, and the baseline records no measurable skew at all.
findings.independence: Offering size, price and use of proceeds from the company's own pricing release, a different document: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/06/30/3319356/36226/en/Mama-s-Creations-Announces-Pricing-of-100-Million-Public-Offering-of-Common-Stock.html . Shares the EDGAR-index absence with the finding above.

findings.finding: The one customer-side datapoint published after MAMA last spoke cuts the other way: Albertsons on 2026-07-23 cut its FY2026 identical-sales outlook from 0.0%-1.0% to (1.5)%-(0.5)% and cut EBITDA guidance, reporting identical sales -0.8% for the 16 weeks ended 2026-06-20 and citing 'core grocery... increasing pressure from softer industry unit trends and a more cautious consumer' - a window that sits inside MAMA's May-July fiscal Q2, on a company whose banners are perimeter-deli customers.
findings.why_not_priced: It was priced into ACI, not into MAMA. MAMA's equity story is door count and new-item wins, so its 2-to-5-estimate consensus is built bottom-up off distribution, not off grocery unit trends; nobody publishing on MAMA has cited a grocer's id-sales guide-down. If MAMA holders had connected it, the stock's August decline would have had commentary attached to it rather than being described in the only note I could find on the pullback as investors 'misinterpreting financial metrics'.
findings.independence: none pointing the same way - and the honest opposite is worth stating: Costco reported July 2026 fresh foods up mid-single digits with meat among the better departments (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/05/3339743/0/en/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-July-Sales-Results.html), and Costco is the likelier identity of the single customer that was 39% of MAMA gross revenue in Q1. That offset is why this finding is sized at -1.5 and not larger.

baseline_tension: My positive number cuts directly against the baseline's run-up (-8.3% 5d, -15.8% 20d, -25.6% from the high) and that is the whole point - it agrees with the only directional thing the option market says out loud here (0.61 put/call open interest, i.e. call-heavy, and no measurable 25-delta skew), so the tape and the chain disagree with each other and I am siding with the chain, while sizing at ~a third of the plausible move because the strongest leg of my case is quoted from a public transcript.
